pairs.subject: candidate-communication-integrity
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/comms-dispatch.ts:73 The dispatcher's recipient cascade falls back from contact to display name, candidate id and the literal "candidate" with no shape check, and WebhookChannel.send (comms.ts) posts whatever it gets to the relay (only SmtpChannel checks isDeliverableAddress), so an unaddressable candidate is handed to transport rather than dead-lettered at the boundary, and the cascade is a second copy of comms-recipient.resolveCandidateRecipient.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/comms-dispatch.ts:73 Name and opaque-id tiers are not addresses; there is no tier stored on the row; the relay path does no shape validation before transport (comms.ts WebhookChannel). It also duplicates the cascade in comms-recipient.ts (a test pins the two equal), so there are two resolvers. The agent refusal is the only tier-4 short-circuit.

app/_lib/comms-status.ts:35 There is one closed enum with queued declared terminal, and coerceOutboxStatus maps unknown values to failed. Caveat: dispatchOutcome re-derives the claim inline instead of calling deliveryClaim, and delivered() lets a queued row write *_sent timeline events.

app/_lib/comms-view.ts:217 latestOkAt counts any non-failed row, including a queued row and a sent row that later bounced, so a dead letter is marked 'recovered' with no external acceptance behind it. Also at line 167, a receipt that is stamped before its send row is never bound to that send, which breaks the arrival-order rule.

app/_lib/comms-dispatch.ts:94 The three-step authority is used and links are ?lang= pinned. But the composition path drops which step supplied the locale, and recordOutbox has no locale field, so a message never records its locale or that locale's source.

app/_lib/comms-dispatch.ts:232 The legal footer links are absolute through candidateLinkBase, which warns loudly when it falls back to the default origin. The footer is never dropped except for erased entries.
app/_lib/comms.ts:350 Escalation is a console line plus comms.log, which ops-telemetry only counts. Nothing routes a dead letter to a human on a clock, and the row does not carry the attempt count.

pairs.evidence: app/_lib/comms-resend-outcome.ts:66 Any 2xx resend whose body carries no recognised entry status (an absent entry, or a status outside queued/failed/bounced) falls through to 'sent', so an unmappable outcome licenses the word Resent instead of resolving to the adverse member.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/comms-resend-outcome.ts:66 The technique says an unmapped transport result must be treated as failed, not sent. Here the default branch is the optimistic resend.

app/_lib/comms-locale.ts:47 The recorded → workspace → app-default authority is correct and resolveCommsLocaleWithSource exists. But the only production entry point discards `source`, and grep finds no non-test caller of the WithSource form, so no message records which step supplied its locale.

app/_lib/comms-recipient.ts:102 The shared cascade resolves display names and opaque ids as recipients. bulk-invite.ts does report unaddressable as its own bucket (conformant there), but the resolver itself does not return a tier and does not shape-validate.

app/_lib/comms-receipt.ts:168 A deferred or soft outcome is answered not_a_bounce and records nothing ("opened"/"deferred" are accepted and not surfaced), so a green sent stands over an attempt the relay reported as not delivered. The technique says a soft bounce stays adverse until something ends it.

app/_lib/comms-receipt.ts:177 A receipt naming nothing kp issued is attached to no tenant but counted install-wide. An unmatched receipt for a known ref is stored and reported as no_matching_send. Only the orphan-receipt half is judged here.

techniques.evidence: app/api/comms/[id]/resend/route.ts:134 This is the `??` address fallback at a call site that the technique bans. A malformed correction is neither refused nor reported.
